text:
maria_cs: Morning team — quick account pulse for Skylift (weekly). TL;DR: 5xx rate jumped this week, timeouts doubled, and we’re seeing a small but growing number of 429s. Need triage and short mitigation plan before renewal touch next week.

High-level metrics (7d vs prior 7d):
- overall error-rate: 5.6% -> 9.8%
- 5xx (server) contrib: +3.4 percentage points (now 7.6% of requests)
- timeouts (gateway upstream): x2 (mostly GET /internal/prefix-cache timeouts)
- rate limits (429): 0.8% -> 1.5% (concentrated on /v1/embeddings)

Top failing endpoints (24h):
1) POST /v1/generate — 52% of 5xx, p50 latency 420ms, p95 1.2s
2) POST /v1/chat — 18% of 5xx, occasional 502s
3) POST /v1/embeddings — 14% errors, ~70% are 429s when they burst
4) GET /internal/prefix-cache — timeouts (context deadline) during their long prefix lookups

Context: Skylift ramped a new ingestion pipeline last Tue, traffic up ~3x for short bursts. They are on Dedicated pool d-pool-7. Renewal check: flagged as "watch" if we don’t stabilize errors before next customer success call.

Can @jess_eng and @tom_infra validate root cause and propose immediate mitigations? I can coordinate comms and update renewal tracker.

sam_success: Noted — I’ll hold the renewal call tentative and prep a short update for their technical contact. If we can get a mitigation in the next 4 hours I’ll keep renewal low-risk.

oncall-bot: ALERT: Skylift customer_id=skylift-207 — 5xx rate exceeded 5% threshold for 12m. Incident link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/INC-2129998887

jess_eng: Looking now. Early signal looks like memory pressure on a subset of nodes in d-pool-7 causing upstream 502s + some handler timeouts. Quick log snippet from 2026-03-18T09:12:14Z:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] runtime: inference-node-7 OOM killer invoked, process restart
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] proxy: upstream error from 10.12.7.9:502 "bad gateway" for /v1/generate (req_id=aa12)
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] gateway: context deadline exceeded after 10s for /internal/prefix-cache (req_id=aa13)
[2026-03-18T09:12:15Z] quota: rate limit applied -> 429 for /v1/embeddings (burst spike)
```

jess_eng: Hypothesis: their bursty workloads and long prefix cache lookups are causing memory thrash on the larger model instances -> OOM restarts -> 502/timeouts. The 429s are orthogonal (client-side burst hitting our per-route qps cap).

tom_infra: Agree with jess. Quick mitigations I can do right now:
- temporarily route Skylift traffic for generate/chat to a smaller quantized model (gpt-small-q4) to reduce per-request memory.
- increase d-pool-7 autoscale max by +20% for 1h to absorb current burst.
- apply per-tenant smoothing: limit Skylift burst to 10 rps sustained (we can relax after they finish ingest).
Commands I’ll run:
```
rwctl routing set --customer skylift-207 --route /v1/generate --fallback gpt-small-q4 --duration 1h
rwctl pool update d-pool-7 --max-instances +20% --duration 1h
rwctl quota set --customer skylift-207 --burst-cap 10
```

jess_eng: I’ll push a runtime guard to catch OOM earlier and return a 503 fallback so proxy doesn’t keep retrying and causing cascading failures. Rolling a canary to one node in d-pool-7 now, will monitor. ETA ~25m.

oliver_se: From an enablement/ops perspective, could CS ask Skylift to:
- add short-circuit caching on their end for prefix matches
- reduce prompt/prefix size for embeddings temporarily
I can draft a 2-paragraph note and a sample cache config snippet if you want.

oliver_se: sample cache header suggestion:
```
cache-control: max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=30
x-prefix-hint: true
```

maria_cs: That sounds like a good plan. @sam_success I’ll send Skylift a quick status update saying we’ve applied temporary routing to a smaller model, increased capacity, and are rolling a runtime guard. Ask them to pause heavy prefix rebuilds for 2 hours and we’ll reassess.

sam_success: Copy. I’ll message them now and include the cache hints + a short SLO note. Also logging this in renewal tracker with "mitigated - monitoring".

oncall-bot: NOTE: Incident INC-2129998887 status -> mitigation applied (routing fallback + autoscale). Monitor for recurrences.

jess_eng: Canary looks good so far, one canary node handled requests without OOM for last 6m. If stable I’ll roll to 25% of d-pool-7 in the next 20m.

tom_infra: Done with routing fallback and autoscale bump. Watching metrics.

maria_cs: Great — thanks everyone. I’ll update the renewal risk to "low->watch" and follow up in tomorrow’s checkin. :thumbsup:
